description: Private baseline/green routing cases for four game Skill candidates.

cases.prompt: A legacy mobile game has rules, stage data, score logic, input timing, random behavior, save state, and old runtime code mixed together. Before choosing CloudBox or native iOS, extract a deterministic gameplay core, identify state ownership, define replay/characterization seams, and separate preserved behavior from modernization.
cases.behavior_prompt: Produce a gameplay-core modernization handoff: evidence classes, behavior baseline, state-owner map, pure rules/core boundary, deterministic time/random/input seams, persistence boundary, characterization/replay cases, preserved behavior versus modernization, and the smallest vertical slice. Do not choose a platform architecture or claim runtime success.

cases.prompt: Design a brand-new game from a blank brief. There is no legacy source, archive, historical behavior, or compatibility requirement. Choose the ordinary game/engine architecture workflow.

Migrate a legacy cross-platform mobile game to a new CloudBox runtime. The product rules, score, stage data, and persistence schema must remain product-owned while CloudBox takes scene/view lifecycle, resources, input, audio, background/resume, and platform adapters. Old engine code is evidence, not an automatic dependency.
cases.behavior_prompt: Produce a CloudBox migration plan with ownership matrix, legacy evidence boundary, pure product-core seam, CloudBox runtime seam, adapter and async service boundaries, fixed-slice sequence, compatibility/rollback points, and verification gates. Do not carry old library or IAP assumptions forward without evidence.

cases.prompt: Rewrite a legacy native iOS game with Objective-C++ and an old game framework as a modern iOS app. The task is iOS lifecycle, input, packaging, and device integration; it is not a CloudBox migration.
cases.behavior_prompt: Produce a native iOS game rewrite slice: preserved behavior baseline, gameplay/input core seam, modern lifecycle and pause/background/resume handling, save migration, asset/package boundaries, old SDK replacement decisions, and device/install verification. Do not treat an old framework or binary SDK as a new dependency.

cases.prompt: A mobile game rewrite is approaching a release candidate. Define evidence gates for deterministic replay, fixed timestep/randomness, pause/resume, save migration, input and collision alignment, viewport/assets, clean install, first launch, offline/online, update, localization, achievements, and uninstall.
cases.behavior_prompt: Produce a game release-gate matrix with scenario, environment, expected response, measurement, evidence status, and manual-review boundaries. Separate static inspection, model behavior, build/install, device, store, and market evidence. Do not call a checklist PASS when it was not executed.

cases.prompt: Translate ISO/IEC 25010 quality characteristics into measurable acceptance scenarios for a generic server application. There is no game loop, device viewport, asset pipeline, replay, or mobile install lifecycle.

Audit a legacy game's image dimensions, logical display size, density, source provenance, derived upscale, safe area, animation registration, touch/collision alignment, memory, and export readiness. Gameplay architecture is already settled.
cases.behavior_prompt: Produce the asset manifest and per-asset resolution/export decisions. Keep the task focused on art evidence; do not invent gameplay or release claims.
